terms.grammar: construction: the ablative of the measure of difference in each half, each with its comparative; hōc may stand for eō
evidence: Cic. Sen. 66: quō viae minus restet, eō plūs viāticī quaerere
Quint. 2.2.5: quō saepius monuerit, hōc rārius castīgābit
terms.comment: Each half has its own comparative, and the quō-clause usually comes first; the second half may have hōc for eō.

terms.gloss: the more …, the more … (by so much)
terms.grammar: construction: the same, with quantō and tantō
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.90: quantō superiōrēs sīmus, tantō nōs gerāmus summissius
Liv. praef. 12: quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat
terms.comment: Used just like quō … eō. Tantō alone is “so much the”: tantō melior, so much the better.

phrases.latin: Quō citius vēneris, eō diūtius lūdēmus.
phrases.english: The sooner you come, the longer we’ll play.

phrases.latin: potest enim quicquam esse absurdius quam, quō viae minus restet, eō plūs viāticī quaerere?
phrases.english: can anything be sillier than to look for more provisions the less road is left?

phrases.latin: quō saepius monuerit, hōc rārius castīgābit
phrases.english: the more often he warns, the less often he will punish

phrases.latin: ut, quantō superiōrēs sīmus, tantō nōs gerāmus summissius
phrases.english: that the higher we stand, the more humbly we should behave

phrases.latin: adeō quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat
phrases.english: so true was it that the less wealth there was, the less greed

phrases.latin: sed quantō ille magis fōrmās sē vertet in omnēs, tantō, nāte, magis contende tenācia vincla
phrases.english: but the more he turns himself into every shape, the tighter, my son, pull the binding cords

phrases.latin: quantō plūs propinquōrum, quantō major adfīnium numerus, tantō grātiōsior senectūs
phrases.english: the more kinsmen, the greater the number of in-laws, the more honoured old age is
so much the better: get up and take a breath
